Subject: SLO variance request for May campaign (p50/p95 measurement windows)

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking a look. We're ramping up a large marketing send the week of May 12–14 and expect short, high-QPS bursts that will push our hosted inference traffic well above baseline for several 3–4 hour windows each day. We've attached traffic samples and the campaign runbook so you can see the schedule.

Ask: Can Redwood provide a temporary variance to the hosted API p95 SLO for the advertised peak windows (detailed below) while preserving p50 commitments and the overall availability SLA? Specifically we'd like to propose:

- Temporary p95 uplift of up to +40% over the current contractual threshold for the listed peak windows only.
- Maintain p50 at current contractual target.
- Rolling measurement: allow defined peak windows to be excluded from rolling-hour penalties if accompanied by evidence.

Planned peak windows (PDT):
- May 12, 2027 — 11:00–15:00
- May 13, 2027 — 12:00–16:00
- May 14, 2027 — 11:30–14:30

Attachments (sample): Finacity_traffic_peaks_May2027.csv (CSV) and campaign_runbook_May2027.pdf (PDF).

Questions for Redwood:
1) What exact evidence and telemetry do you need to accept a temporary windowed variance (latency histograms, token distribution, trace IDs)?
2) What guardrails will Redwood require to ensure this doesn't create platform-wide regressions (fallback models, throttling, auto-degrade)?
3) Timeline: we need a signed amendment by May 10 to be operational for May 12. Is that feasible?

We're happy to join a short alignment call — suggested times Tue/Wed next week afternoon PT.

Best,
Sofia Patel
SLA Manager — Finacity

Hi Sofia — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments; I skimmed the runbook and CSV. We can probably support a temporary, narrowly scoped variance, but we'll need a compact evidence package and a tight operational playbook from both sides. To keep things moving, here's what I need from you by EOD May 8: 

Required from Finacity (minimum evidence set)
- Hourly latency histograms (p10/p50/p90/p95) for a recent 7-day baseline window, ideally with request size / token distribution attached.
- A CSV of expected QPS by minute for each peak day (you've started this; we need completeness).
- A short-runbook section on fallback behavior on your side (e.g., client-side backoff, retry budget).

What Redwood will provide
- A proposed measurement approach (see below) and a draft amendment for review.
- Implementation guardrails: canary rollout in a single region first, automatic fallback to a lower-throughput model variant if p95 exceeds an agreed emergency ceiling, and an alerting playbook.

Proposed measurement approach (high-level) — I'll let Karthik follow up with specifics, but rough idea:
- Maintain contractual p50 target across all windows.
- For p95, support a windowed variance where defined peak windows are evaluated against a short rolling measurement window and qualified based on provided evidence.
- Variance will be limited in duration and capped by an absolute emergency ceiling (e.g., 600ms) to protect other tenants.

Next steps
- Karthik, can you outline the measurement bucket alignment and the telemetry we'll require?
- Hannah, I'll need legal/contract help drafting a short amendment (term + dates + ceiling + rollback triggers).

Sofia — if you can get the 7-day histograms and completed QPS-by-minute spreadsheet to us by EOD May 8 we’ll target a draft amendment on May 9 and a DocuSign-ready version by May 10. Scheduling: Tue 5/11 10:00–10:30 PT works for me to finalize.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: SLO variance request for May campaign (p50/p95 measurement windows) — measurement proposal

Hi all — quick technical proposal for how Redwood would evaluate/qualify the temporary p95 variance requested by Finacity. I kept it intentionally prescriptive so legal can encode it in the amendment.

1) Measurement windows and aggregation
- Baseline: compute latency quantiles (p50/p95) on a sliding 1-hour window sampled every 15 minutes (overlapping windows).
- Peak qualification: designate explicit peak windows (start/end timestamps as agreed) — metrics during those windows may be excluded from rolling penalty calculation only if Finacity provides the evidence set (listed below).
- Emergency ceiling: irrespective of variance, absolute p95 must not exceed 600ms for any 5-minute bucket; this is an automatic rollback trigger.

2) SLO thresholds (example numbers — will be replaced by contract values)
- Baseline contractual targets: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 300ms.
- Requested variance allowance: allow measured p95 to be up to 40% higher than contractual p95 during designated peak windows, but capped at 600ms.

3) Required telemetry/evidence
- Latency histograms by minute for the baseline 7-day window (CSV or JSONL).
- Token-distribution by request (sample 1% or min 1k requests) — attached file prefix-token-distribution.csv would be ideal.
- Request traces for any outlier minute where p95 > 1.25x baseline during a peak window (to support root cause).

4) Operational guardrails
- Canary: enforce the variance in a single region for the first peak window; promote to multi-region only if canary metrics meet expectations.
- Auto-fallback: if p95 > emergency ceiling (600ms) for 5 consecutive minutes, Redwood will automatically route new requests to a fallback model variant and notify on-call.
- Communication: Finacity must provide per-minute QPS during peak windows at least 6 hours before the window start for Redwood to decide capacity & prioritization.

5) Rollback and audit
- Any invocation of the emergency rollback will be logged and reported within 30 minutes.
- Finacity may request a post-mortem if rollback occurs during the campaign.

If that all sounds ok to Laura/legal/Finacity I can turn the numbers into contract language. Attaching a sample CSV (prefix-token-distribution.csv) to indicate the shape of data we need.

—Karthik
Principal Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: prefix-token-distribution.csv (text/csv)
